question: In September 2024, the Indian government constituted a high-level committee headed by which individual to examine the feasibility and implementation of the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ram Nath Kovind**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In September 2024, the Indian government formed a high-level committee to explore the feasibility and implementation of the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal.
 
• The committee is chaired by **Ram Nath Kovind**, the former President of India.
 
• The 'One Nation, One Election' proposal aims to synchronize elections for the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, Panchayats, and Urban Local Bodies to reduce electoral costs and disruptions.
 
• Ram Nath Kovind was chosen to lead this effort due to his experience and knowledge of constitutional and governance matters.
 
• This initiative reflects the government's intention to streamline electoral processes and improve governance efficiency in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One Nation, One Election:**

 
 
• It is a proposal to hold simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and local bodies to ensure uniformity and reduce frequent disruptions caused by election processes.
 
• The concept aims to save resources, both financial and administrative, while maintaining the focus on governance.
 
• Implementing this proposal requires significant constitutional amendments and consensus among political parties.
 
 
 
• **Ram Nath Kovind:**
 
 
• Ram Nath Kovind served as the 14th President of India from July 25, 2017, to July 25, 2022.
 
• He was also a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha and Governor of Bihar before assuming the presidential role.
 
• Known for his legal acumen, Kovind has extensive experience in constitutional matters.
 
 
 
• **Electoral Costs and Challenges:**
 
 
• Frequent elections result in high financial costs, including expenses for security, logistics, and administration.
 
• They also cause disruptions in governance, as the model code of conduct restricts policy decisions during election periods.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• Synchronizing elections would require amendments to Articles 83, 85, 172, 174, and 356 of the Constitution, among others.
 
• It would also necessitate changes to Representation of People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Previous Discussions:**
 
 
• The 'One Nation, One Election' idea has been discussed multiple times since 2014, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi advocating its merits.
 
• The Law Commission of India also explored its feasibility in its 2018 report.
